## Overview

Traditional R web applications (such as local Shiny dashboards) spin up an HTTP server and bind to a local TCP/IP port (e.g. `127.0.0.1:8100`). In locked-down enterprise environments or isolated field machines, this often triggers corporate firewall warnings, port collision conflicts, or security policy violations.

**RDesk rethinks local R application delivery from the ground up:**

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### 🔒 Firewall & Port Immune
Zero HTTP servers and zero open sockets. All bidirectional communication between R and the user interface occurs over OS pipes via native C++ IPC.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### 📦 Standalone Binaries
Package your entire application into a single `.zip` distribution or installer containing a matching portable R runtime and all package dependencies. Users don't need R installed!
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### ⚡ Non-Blocking Async
Powered by background worker processes (`callr` / `mirai`), long-running calculations, data exports, and heavy plotting never freeze the user interface.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### 🎨 Modern Web UI
Build rich interfaces using modern HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, or take advantage of our pre-built responsive dashboard templates with dark and light modes.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Windows Release Focus
RDesk v1.0.7 is fully optimized for Windows desktop environments leveraging the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime. Inert cross-platform scaffolding is underway with native macOS (WebKit) and Linux (WebKitGTK) support planned for subsequent releases.
:::

## Quick Start

### 1. Create an Application

Generate a fully functional, production-ready desktop dashboard in one command:

```r
# Scaffold a modern dashboard app
RDesk::rdesk_create_app("SalesAnalytics", theme = "dark")
```

### 2. Run in Development Mode

Navigate to your application directory and launch it:

```r
setwd("SalesAnalytics")
source("app.R")
```

During development, `rdesk_watch()` enables live hot-reloading: whenever you edit an HTML, CSS, or JS file in `www/`, your WebView2 window automatically refreshes!

### 3. Build a Standalone Executable

When you are ready to distribute your app to clients or colleagues:

```r
RDesk::build_app(
  app_dir  = "SalesAnalytics",
  app_name = "SalesAnalytics",
  version  = "1.0.0"
)
```

RDesk stages your app files, copies your active R runtime, snapshots dependencies, compiles a native launcher stub, and generates `SalesAnalytics-1.0.0-windows.zip` ready for distribution.
